title: Type switches
hints: A type switch, switch v := x.(type) { case int: … }, picks a case by the dynamic type stored in an interface, and inside each case v has that type.

Cases are checked top to bottom, and a case can name an interface such as fmt.Stringer. `case nil:` matches an interface holding nothing at all. Put the Stringer case after the concrete types if you want them to win.

switch v := x.(type) { case nil: return "nil"; case int: return fmt.Sprintf("int %d", v); case string: return fmt.Sprintf("string %q", v); case []int: return fmt.Sprintf("%d ints", len(v)); case fmt.Stringer: return "stringer " + v.String(); default: return "unknown" }
